part.name: BBa_262YYNPV
part.title: AcdS 2.1
part.description: This part encodes 1-aminocyclopropane-1-carboxylate (ACC) deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* (Arthrobacter siderocapsulatus) strain UW4; ; the wild-type acdS sequence is registered as [BBa\_26MA70QI](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26ma70qi). It is an enzyme commonly found in plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR). ACC deaminase degrades ACC, the precursor of the plant hormone ethylene, thereby alleviating ethylene-induced growth inhibition in plants under stress. In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

documentation.title: Design
documentation.value:
## **About**

* **Biosafety level:** S1 
* **Target organism:** *Bacillus subtilis* \[168 / WB800] 
*  In this variant, the first 15 codons of the coding sequence were optimized to improve the mRNA secondary structure of the translation start site.

## **Literature**

The cloned ACC deaminase gene can be expressed in *Escherichia coli*, which enables this bacterium to grow on ACC as its sole nitrogen source. Both *E. coli* and *Pseudomonas* spp. strains transformed with this gene gain the ability to promote root elongation in canola seedlings (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

A soluble recombinant ACC deaminase from *Pseudomonas putida* UW4 was cloned, expressed and purified. It has a molecular weight of 41 kDa and shows selectivity and high activity towards ACC, with a K(M)\=3.4+/-0.2 mM and k(cat)\=146+/-5 min(-1) at pH 8.0 and 22 °C. Activity is optimal at pH 8.0 and declines sharply to essentially nothing below pH 6.5. It tapers off more gradually at higher pH, and activity is lost above pH 10. (Hontzeas et al., 2004).

## Dry lab / computational analysis



![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/4d2952c4-918d-457f-9c1e-28a43b67a40a/90114dd860dc6aab37a0a03c1cd55703179ba9dc9155ad3c299f3cf4f6dc28c4.avif)

**Figure ST-1. ACC deaminase, the enzyme this cassette secretes.** (a) The fold of ACC deaminase, drawn from PDB 1TZJ chain A (Pseudomonas sp. ACP, X-ray, 1.99 Å). This is the closest experimentally determined structure to our own acdS: 83 % identical over 330 aligned residues. It is a structural reference for the fold and the active site — it is not a model of our exact protein, and no structure of our acdS has been determined. (b) The active site. The pyridoxal-5′-phosphate cofactor (orange) is held by a Schiff base to Lys51, which aligns to Lys50 in our sequence and is conserved. D-vinylglycine (green), a substrate analogue, sits in the pocket where ACC binds. Teal side chains are the residues within 4.2 Å of the ligand, computed from the coordinates: Ser78, Tyr268, Tyr294. ACC deaminase cleaves ACC, the immediate precursor of the plant stress hormone ethylene. Secreted into the root zone it lowers ethylene and reduces the growth penalty plants pay under salt stress.

![](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/4d2952c4-918d-457f-9c1e-28a43b67a40a/6e350dfaf39fc20734e7742d6aea874e610db87b48945c1d77c160d6e2d1a16b.avif)

**Figure CO-1. Translation-initiation structure of the ACCD v2 top1 cassette.** (a) The ordered design against the wild type, a naive low-GC recoding rule, and the best candidates of a replicate 50,000-variant search; it ranks 3 of 49,987, the top 0.006 % of the pool. (b) Predicted minimum-free-energy secondary structure of the wild-type messenger RNA window — 236 nt: recombination site, MF001 ribosome binding site, SamyQ signal peptide and the first 90 nt of the coding sequence — at -42.1 kcal/mol. (c) The same for the ordered design at -49.7 kcal/mol; the 15 bases that differ from wild type are orange. (d) Probability that each base is unpaired, wild type in grey against the ordered design in green, with the ribosome binding site, the start+15 window and the recoded region shaded. Start-codon accessibility 0.563 → 0.773; ribosome-binding-site accessibility 0.088 → 0.203. All 12 codon changes are synonymous — the protein (NLNRFERYPLTFGPS…) and the SamyQ cleavage site are unchanged. ViennaRNA 2.7.2, 37 °C, partition function, noLonelyPairs on.

documentation.title: Application
documentation.value:
This part was designed for the GEMS-Taiwan 2026 iGEM team’s work on a Stress-Responsive Optogenetic Bioreactor for Precision Plant Protection and is used in the construction of composite parts:

* **SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag** ([<u>**BBa\_26TOGLX3**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26toglx3))**:** The ACC deaminase protein is fused to the alpha-amylase signal peptide (SamyQ) at the N-terminus and a 6x Histag at the C-terminus.\*\*\*\* 
* **Pveg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([<u>**BBa\_26XVQ3FS**</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xvq3fs)): this **Protectant Module** constitutively expresses potential stress-mitigation proteins and enables evaluation of their secretion and detection, with its constitutive promoter Pveg, RBS EEBD-RBS, and terminator B0015.
* **PcpcG2-veg-EEBD-RBS0-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag-B0015** ([BBa\_263IW021](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-263iw021)): this module includes the light-responsive promoter P*cpcG2*-veg, the RBS EEBD-RBS0, a protectant CDS, and the terminator B0015, which together drive the expression of downstream genes in response to green-light signaling in *Bacillus Subtilis* after[<u>BBa\_26XZYM10</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26xzym10),[<u>BBa\_261XH2RS</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-261xh2rs), and[<u>BBa\_26BDO8AQ</u>](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26bdo8aq).
* **ccaSR-SamyQ-AcdS 2.1-Histag** ([BBa\_26RF0X2E](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26rf0x2e)): the system is an engineered construct that produces and secretes plant-protective proteins under green/red light control.
